EDIT-SET CLOSURE BANKED AS THE DISPOSITION OF THE REPEATED-CLASS ORDER, AND IT CAUGHT A SECOND SITE ON ITS FIRST RUN 2026-10-03: the operator order was that the same defects must stop repeating so the goal arrives faster. The disposition is deliberately NOT a fourth clause of the shape already banked, because this round proved that shape cannot see these defects - every earlier gate tested an ARTIFACT while the recurrence was a RELATION between artifacts - and the honest disposition of a repeated class after a gate for it exists is a check of a different shape over the same phase, with the bypassed gate named. The new gate has three mechanical parts and all three ran on v18. (1) FINGERPRINT CLOSURE: every phrase a fold replaces takes a six-word fingerprint and the whole page is searched for it; a fingerprint surviving on any line other than its own edited line is a MISSED CELL and the fold is blocked. On its first run it found two carried sections - the V396 binding-requirements paragraph and the function-return-census requirement - still saying g_evictBits writes where the controlling section had just classified twelve touch points as two declarations, four clears, two bit-set writers and four reads; three further fingerprints were proved to survive only on their own edited lines. (2) PROMISE-RESOLUTION: every normative promise phrase must have its referent asserted present by count on the same page, which is what the two promises without homes in the acceptance needed. (3) LIST RE-CLASSIFICATION: every enumerated EA-line list inside a sentence is re-derived from the EA at fold time and its classification printed beside it, and the sentence is accepted only when the mechanical classification and the printed one agree - that check classified EA 1939 and EA 1940 as declarations, EA 1965, EA 1971, EA 8111 and EA 8116 as clears, EA 9323 and EA 9325 as the only bit-set writers, EA 1961, EA 1967, EA 8112 and EA 8117 as reads, and EA 2121, EA 2143 and EA 11968 as += writes of counters that are RETAINED. The mislabelled history lines were left verbatim because carried history is never rewritten; 15.6 now declares the earlier phrasing superseded and names the classification that governs. Second-order ownership is banked with it: when a defect class repeats after a gate for it, the disposition is a differently shaped check and the ledger names which gate was bypassed and why it could not see that instance. srj-council measured after the edit at 63CEB932441C1D94D182356C28D27B728F22E0CC66B34D2CA8D6449BBE49DE38/135590 B/509 LF, each of the three new part names counted once. srj-defect needed no new clause this round because the repeated class here is a page-relation class owned by srj-council, not a verification-discipline class; srj-strategy and srj-goal were checked and unchanged, since no pin moved, no strategy meaning changed and no run or goal metric moved. The machine buying at 15:35 (159.774, aiming at the 30 April high) is answering a touch I do not count. And a correction to how the question was framed: what do you mean by "my 5m view is against it" — the 5m structure? A POI line retest does not go stale, and it is not invalidated, by a five-minute bias flip. This is the same misunderstanding as the previous planner mistake that took the B-61 ruling to fix: a retest on the flip candle stays a potential and is judged at the confirmation candle. Never use my 5m read to age a retest or to kill a line. The 5m flip rule kills a formed setup before confirmation — it does not touch retest validity." ANSWER 6/10: "2. 10 June — valid retest, then invalidated before confirmation. The machine should have stayed out. Yes, the 15:30 candle is a valid retest of the Daily POC. But the 15:45 candle invalidated it with a candle body closure over the line: 15:45 opened 160.394 and closed 160.351, straight through the Daily POC at 160.354. Dead is dead. There was nothing left to confirm at 16:05, and the 16:10 buy at 160.436 should never have fired. The machine's own rows agree with my chart here — it logged the 15:45 close under the line and kept the seed alive anyway. I have not ruled on this exact candle before, but no new ruling is needed: apply my standing words. A retest that breaks its POI lines with a candle body close before the confirmation entry is invalidated (my 16:05-venue words), exactly like the 8/27 18:05 retest dying on the 18:10 and 18:15 closes. The rule is the rule — same scenario class, same verdict: INVALID, no take." STANDING INSTRUCTION: "A standing instruction, not a question. Stop inventing behavior for the EA. Its behavior is set, and I have explained it to you across these rulings: retests die by body-close breaks, never by 5m flips. When I talk to the builder directly there is no such hallucination, because the builder answers from my banked words plus the code rows. Do the same: quote my words, point at rows, and do not re-decide the logic."
